findings: Fail-closed classification verified: worker-level COMPLETE is never promoted to scientific VALIDATED; dispatch success maps only from DISPATCHED_NOT_YET_VALIDATED; all unknown statuses default to FAILED.

At-most-once dispatch preserved: dispatch-phase timeouts, failures, and expired-lease recoveries all block with AMBIGUOUS_DISPATCH_CHECK_REMOTE_BEFORE_RETRY; no auto-retry path exists for the side-effecting phase, and complete_event rejects any direct dispatch-to-VALIDATED transition.

Recovery semantics fenced: stale completions rejected via lease equality; duplicate event ids are idempotent while conflicting replays raise; read-only retry cap of 2 enforced consistently in both claim recovery and TRANSIENT completion paths; patient-phase VALIDATED blocks for human transfer rather than auto-publishing.

Identity binding immutable: register rejects rebinding a job id to different inputs; snapshot() accepts only the hardcoded approved pin with HEAD equality and clean worktree; workers execute from the pinned snapshot cwd; coordinator files re-hashed against the review record on every tick, fail-closed on mismatch or missing hash.

Privacy boundaries hold: only a fixed result enum persists in sqlite; worker stdout/stderr confined to a 0700/0600 private root created under umask 077, refused if symlinked or resolving inside the checkout; no worker output or sensitive paths printed to coordinator stdout.

Minor (non-blocking): git rev-parse on the full 40-hex SNAPSHOT_PIN in ROOT does not verify object existence; harmless because the check is equality against the hardcoded constant, but --verify <pin>^{commit} would be stricter.
Minor (non-blocking): status/tick on an unregistered job raises an unhandled TypeError from dict(None) in Store.get; fail-closed but should produce a clean error.
Minor (non-blocking): git status --porcelain does not flag gitignored files in the snapshot worktree; --ignored would give stricter drift detection.

Caveat (non-blocking): the at-most-once dispatch guarantee is per store file; two coordinators launched with distinct --private-root stores could each register the same experiment and double-dispatch; needs an operational safeguard outside this code.

Minor (non-blocking): snapshot() git subprocesses have no timeout, so a hung git call stalls a tick past the lease; stale-lease fencing prevents state corruption but the run loop would rely on the ambiguous-dispatch block after recovery.
Minor (non-blocking): demo writes a SYNTHETIC job and OPEN inbox entry into the production store; clearly labeled but pollutes inbox listings.
